newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha flat despite bullish crudes.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha flat despite bullish crudes.

text.p: Naphtha prices barely moved in afternoon trade on Wednesday despite moderate gains in overnight crude prices, traders said.
This was in sharp contrast with Monday's bullish Tokyo naphtha market, which shrugged off Friday's overseas crude losses, they added.
"Naphtha has been very strong for quite a while," one trader said. "Now it's in a correctional phase."
Open-spec naphtha for second-half April was assessed at $232.50/233.50, little changed from $233.00/234.00 in late Tuesday dealing.
In Tuesday trading, second-half May was traded once at $225.00, again at $225.25, and once again at $225.50.
In spreads, second-half April/second-half May was indicated at plus $6.00/7.00, virtually unchanged from Tuesday.

In the low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) market, domestic demand remained slack as it is currently more economical for refiners to manufacture LSWR domestically by processing regional crudes than importing LSWR cargoes, traders said.
